name: Soldering Iron Kit (adjustable)
desc: Melts solder to join wires and pins permanently. Needed for modules that ship with loose header pins.
note: The tip is about 350°C. Always use the stand, work in a ventilated room, and wash your hands after handling solder.

name: Digital Multimeter
desc: Measures voltage, resistance and continuity (beeps when two points are connected). Your best friend for finding wiring mistakes.
note: Beginner rule: only measure low-voltage circuits (batteries, boards), never wall sockets.

name: Wire Stripper / Cutter
desc: Cuts wire and removes its plastic coating cleanly without nicking the copper.

name: Hot Glue Gun
desc: Sticks your project into its case and holds wires in place. The fastest way to make a build look finished.
note: The nozzle and fresh glue are hot enough to burn skin.

name: Solder Wire (rosin core, 0.8mm)
desc: The metal "glue" for soldering. Rosin core cleans the joint as it melts.
note: Lead-free solder is safer; if you use leaded solder, wash your hands after.

name: Soldering Flux (pen or paste)
desc: Helps solder flow and stick, especially on old or tricky joints.

name: Desoldering Pump
desc: A spring-loaded vacuum that sucks up melted solder to fix mistakes.

name: Helping Hands with Magnifier
desc: Clips that hold parts and boards steady while you solder, plus a magnifying glass.

name: Precision Tweezers (ESD-safe)
desc: For placing tiny parts and bending component legs.

name: Precision Screwdriver Set
desc: Tiny screwdrivers for terminal blocks, potentiometers and cases.

name: Flush Side Cutters
desc: Snips component legs flush against the board after soldering.
note: Point the leg away from your face when cutting: they fly!

name: Needle-Nose Pliers
desc: For bending wires and holding small parts.

name: Dupont Crimping Tool + Connector Kit
desc: Make your own custom-length jumper wires and connectors.

name: USB Logic Analyzer (8-channel)
desc: Records digital signals so you can see what's happening on I2C, SPI and serial lines (with free PulseView software).

name: USB Power Meter (voltage & current)
desc: Plugs between charger and cable to show how much power your project draws.

name: Safety Glasses
desc: Protects your eyes from flying leg clippings and solder splashes. Wear them!

name: Adjustable Bench Power Supply (0–30V, 5A)
desc: A lab power supply with a current limit: the ultimate protection against magic smoke while testing.
note: Set the current limit low (e.g. 100mA) when powering a new circuit for the first time.

name: Silicone Soldering Mat
desc: A heat-resistant mat with trays for screws: protects your desk while soldering.
